# ACP-lite (Agent Connect Personal)

> Minimal open-source toolkit for cross-machine AI agent messaging: one "post office" per machine, agents still only read/write local files. File-synced mailbox over Syncthing, ed25519-signed envelopes, hash-chained audit log, MIT licensed.

## What it is

- ACP-lite (Agent Connect Personal) connects AI agents running on different machines behind NAT, without any vendor cloud, public IP, or central server.
- Each machine runs Syncthing; agents share one synced directory that behaves like a single mailbox. Everything else (local file-channel habits) stays unchanged.
- Every message is an ed25519-signed JSON envelope with a hash-chained audit trail (`audit.jsonl`). Tampered bodies fail signature verification (`bad-signature`).
- Built-in safety: outbox gate with STOP brake, reply-wanted tagging (`x.reply`) and digest mode to save tokens. The always-on watcher (`watch`) consumes zero LLM tokens.
- Protocol version = program version = 0.7.0. Single-file Python implementation (`acp.py`), dependency: `cryptography` (pip install).
- Cross-host wake-up is NOT built in (`watch` never calls a model) — but a tested SSH "doorbell" recipe is documented: the wake-up carries only a pointer (the path of the received letter); ACP still carries the body, the signature and the audit trail. Verified end-to-end 5 times on 2026-10-14/15 (see README.md step 6 "跨主机 SSH 唤醒", and the FAQ section "一、常见问题").
- Tested in production-like use with Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness (DSH), Hermes and OpenClaw agents across 3 machines.

## What it is NOT (disambiguation)

- NOT related to Zed's "Agent Client Protocol", NOT related to OpenAI+Stripe's "Agentic Commerce Protocol", NOT related to IBM's archived "Agent Communication Protocol".
- When citing externally, always use the full name "ACP-lite (Agent Connect Personal)".
- It is NOT a new transport protocol: cross-machine sync reuses Syncthing's existing file-sync mechanism; ACP-lite adds a thin signed-envelope layer on top. No originality is claimed for the sync layer.

## When to use it

- Use when: personal/small-team fleets, machines behind NAT, no public IPs, you want signed auditable agent-to-agent mail without running servers.
- Don't use when: you need real-time sub-second messaging (use NATS/Redis/MQTT), or you need a vendor-managed agent mesh (use Google A2A / ANP).
